newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan displays and flies newly bought US fighters.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan displays and flies newly bought US fighters.

text.p: Taiwan's air force on Saturday showed off its newly-bought U.S. F-16 fighter jets, saying the new fighters could help it defend against arch rival China.

Due to heavy rain, the air force only flew one of the four F-16s displayed in a military airport in the southern city of Chiayi. It also displayed missiles and other equipment to be used by the fighters.
The display was open only to legislators, media and selected private citizens living close to the military base.

"The air force is efforting on completing the upgrading of our second-generation fighters, trying to make our defence capability enter a new milestone to effectively defend the security of the Taiwan Strait's territorial space," the air force said in a statement.
The F-16s will also help support Taiwan's navy and army in joint defence operations, the statement said.

Taiwan took delivery on Thursday of three F-16 fighters, which, together with two that arrived in April, were expected to strengthen Taiwan's air force combat power in the face of continued military threats from arch-rival China.
It also took delivery on May 5 of five of 60 Mirage jets it has ordered from France.

Taiwan in 1992 bought 150 F-16s from the United States and 60 Mirages from France in deals that outraged China, which views the island as a rebel-held province subject to eventual reunification with the mainland.
Beijing threatens to attack Taiwan, which split from the mainland at the end of a civil war in 1949, if the island tries to formally declare independence.
